content:
Hi! I'd like to publicise a small library I threw together recently for fuzzing Lean
DSLs: https://github.com/kiranandcode/lean-fuzz

Lean-Fuzz is a grammar-based fuzzing library for Lean 4. Lean's
extensible syntax means you can't define a single grammar ahead of
time, but its metaprogramming capabilities mean you can extract this
information from the compiler at runtime.

lean-fuzz hooks in via the metaprogramming faciliites to read the
parser extension state from any imported module, extracts the full
grammar (including custom declare_syntax_cat categories), and uses it
to generate random syntactically-guided inputs. For example, pointing
it at https://github.com/leodemoura/RadixExperiment:

  import LeanFuzz
  import Radix

  def main (args : List String) : IO Unit :=
    LeanFuzz.fuzzGrammar #[`Radix] `rstmt args

It also supports dumping the extracted grammar to JSON for use with external tools like AFL++ Grammar Mutator (--dump-grammar afl). The repo has
https://github.com/kiranandcode/lean-fuzz/tree/main/examples/grammars extracted from Radix, Strata, Veil, and Velvet.
I made a much more primitive version of this a while ago so I’m real glad to see this! Thank you
